newsitem.title: USA: McDermott plans to restructure, cut costs.
newsitem.headline: McDermott plans to restructure, cut costs.

text.p: McDermott International Inc plans to cut headquarters costs and restructure corporate operations in a bid to return to profitability by next year, the company's new chief executive officer said on Monday.

The company expects to slash its general and administrative costs to $53 million in fiscal 1998 and $48 million the following year from $67 million this year, CEO Roger Tetrault said on an analysts' conference call.
The company also plans to sell or write off non-core assets and focus on its core marine construction, power generation and government contracting groups, Tetrault said.

The company's 400-person headquarters staff will be cut by at least 95 people, partly through attrition. The company also will end its sponsorship of a New Orleans professional golf tournament and move out of expensive leased space in New Orleans to reduce administrative expenses, he said.
"At a minimum, I expect we will be profitable in fiscal 1998," Tetrault said.

McDermott earlier said it expected to report a $180 million to $200 million net loss in its fiscal fourth quarter compared to a $4 million net loss in the same period last year. Audited results for the year are expected to be released in mid-May.

The company and its J. Ray McDermott unit also are investigating allegations unnamed former employees may have engaged in "wrongdoing." If true, the allegations could result in civil or criminal liability for the companies, it said.
"I will have no comment on the allegations of wrongdoing," Tetrault said on the conference call.

A former senior vice president of General Dynamics Corp, Tetrault was brought in as McDermott's CEO in March to begin turning the ailing engineering and services company around. He will replace Chairman James Dutt in August.
On Thursday, he will begin meeting with the heads of every business unit in the company to review expected results and forecasts for the coming year, he said.
